originality.rationale: The proved claim is the exact order-at-most-six quotient, not an unbounded enumeration. Topological ordering reduces each n-vertex DAG to one of the 2^{n(n-1)/2} forward-arc matrices. A Python verifier explicitly enumerates every matrix and computes synchronized directed in/out refinement, then exact colour-preserving arc-isomorphism via exhaustive backtracking for all candidates within every histogram bucket. A separately implemented C++ canonical-labelling enumeration and Python refinement reproduces all six counts: DAG types (1,2,6,31,302,5984) and C2 types (1,2,6,31,302,5983), with exactly one two-type collision. The explicit pair, two disjoint transitive triangles versus an acyclic orientation of a six-cycle, has identical equitable directed neighbour statistics but differs in connectivity. Standard C2--one-dimensional colour-refinement equivalence for a binary relation applies because loop and reciprocal-arc types are fixed and absent arcs are determined by class sizes and in/out counts.
residual_risks: A previous specialist table of directed colour-refinement ambiguity among small DAGs may exist but was not located.

value.rationale: The natural question whether DAG acyclicity removes the ambiguity of C2 / colour refinement receives its sharp first-failure answer. A complete natural cutoff and first exceptional layer (exactly one pair out of 5984 DAG types) is useful as a mathematical boundary and implementation benchmark, rather than an arbitrary table or recount of the known DAG numbers. The connected-six-cycle versus disconnected-two-triangles witness isolates the structural information that local in/out aggregation loses.
